claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, so a separate domain is not required for the Terraform-compatible API.
The Pulumi state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, login commands, and TF_TOKEN_* variable name.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ exists and documents using Pulumi Cloud as a Terraform/OpenTofu state backend.
